subject: BlueArc: temporary log escrow + CAIQ evidence pathway
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda@bluearchealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-08T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Request: temporary log escrow & CAIQ evidence for forensic retention

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to sign-off internally but Security raised one last ask: for a 90-day period following go-live we need an option to escrow a subset of tenant debug/audit logs for forensic purposes. The ask is narrow — only logs for PII-related incidents and only for a named test tenant — but we need:

- a written pathway that explains how Redwood will preserve and provide those logs on request (chain-of-custody, retention timeline, access controls),
- evidence artifacts mapped to CAIQ/SIG items (we attached our filled CAIQ), and
- a draft SLA/escrow agreement we can attach to our procurement package.

Can you share what artifacts you can provide and an expected delivery timeline? We will need the CAIQ-mapped evidence and a log manifest example for our audit.

Attached: BlueArc-CAIQ-filled.pdf (PDF)

Regards,
Linda Park
Director, Information Security
BlueArc Health

Attachment stub: BlueArc-CAIQ-filled.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@bluearchealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-08T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log escrow & CAIQ evidence for forensic retention

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear ask and the filled CAIQ. We can support a narrow, timeboxed escrow for tenant-scoped logs but want to confirm a couple of scope items up front so we send the right artifacts: 

1) Exact log types: do you need only audit-event + request-trace logs, or also full application debug traces? Our recommended minimum is audited-event + request-trace (those contain the necessary chain-of-custody metadata).
2) Searchability: do you need full-text search-ready exports, or CSV/structured manifests with timestamps and checksums?
3) Access model: will BlueArc require direct SFTP retrieval, or would you prefer a Redwood-hosted secure archive with time-limited access tokens and an attested download process?

What we can commit to deliver within 5 business days after scope confirmation:
- CAIQ mapping document (PDF) that cites which Redwood artifacts satisfy each CAIQ item you flagged,
- a sample log manifest (CSV) showing the fields, timestamp format, and SHA256 checksums for integrity,
- a draft temporary-escrow SLA (PDF) for your legal/procurement team.

I've looped in Rishi (security engineering) and Priya (compliance) to advise on evidence artifacts. If you can confirm the three scope bullets above today, we'll start packaging materials tomorrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs referenced: sample-log-manifest.csv, temporary-escrow-sla-draft.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: BlueArc escrow scope and artifacts (draft)

Kim / Priya — quick internal note before we respond to BlueArc directly. I reviewed their filled CAIQ, and the items they're focusing on map to: 

- CM-8 / Logging retention: we have our default retention policies and can produce signed export snapshots.
- IA-6 / Access controls: we can provide an attestation and the access-control audit trail.
- SI-4 / Integrity checks: we generate per-file SHA256 and can include a time-stamped notarization entry.

Proposed answers & artifacts:
- CAIQ mapping PDF that references our internal artifact IDs (e.g., ARCH-LOG-EXPORT-2027-11), plus a short narrative for each CAIQ claim.
- sample-log-manifest.csv with columns: file_name, tenant_id, time_range_start, time_range_end, sha256, record_count, storage_uri
- chain-of-custody memo (one page) describing our attestation process and the persons authorized to release — signed by SOC contact.
- 90-day escrow SLA: limit to specific tenant ID(s), specify retrieval SLA (48 hours), audit trail delivery, and deletion confirmation (proof-of-delete with checksums).

Operational considerations: we should prefer Redwood-hosted secure archive with pre-signed access links (token expiration) to avoid direct SFTP handoffs. That reduces transfer risk and gives us clear download logs. Priya, can you draft the CAIQ mapping narrative and the chain-of-custody memo? I'll take the sample manifest and the escrow SLA draft.

Rishi
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Linda Park <linda@bluearchealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluearchealth.com
Date: 2027-11-11T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log escrow & CAIQ evidence for forensic retention

Kim / Rishi / Priya — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. To confirm:

- Log types: audit-event + request-trace only (no debug traces).
- Searchability: CSV/manifest with checksums and a limited full-text extract for incident-scoped retrieval is sufficient.
- Access: BlueArc prefers Redwood-hosted secure archive with time-limited access tokens and audit logs of every download.

Procurement would like the draft temporary-escrow SLA and the CAIQ mapping (we will attach both to the SOW). Also: please include an example of the proof-of-delete note we will receive after the 90-day period.

If you can deliver the artifacts and the two-page chain-of-custody memo by EOD Friday (2027-11-12), we'll include them in our final package and move forward. We also received the DocuSign link from procurement and will route the SOW once the attachments are in place.

Thanks again — please send the materials to this thread and to procurement@bluearchealth.com.

Best,
Linda Park
Director, Information Security
BlueArc Health
